Rashi on Shabbat 92b:10:1.hebrew: הוציאו שנים פטורין - כדילפינן בעשותה, יחיד ולא שנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:10:1.english: [If] two carried [it] out, they are exempt - As we derive from [the verse] "in doing it" [Leviticus 4:27]: an individual [is liable], and not two.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:10:2.english: They are liable - And the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:1.hebrew: זה יכול - להוציאו לבדו, וזה יכול להוציאו לבדו, והוציאו שניהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:1.english: This [person] is capable - of carrying it out alone, and that [person] is capable of carrying it out alone, and the two of them carried [it] out.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:2.hebrew: ר"מ מחייב - דלא דריש בעשותה להכי, אלא לפטור יחיד שעשה בהוראת ב"ד, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:2.english: Rabbi Meir deems [them] liable - For he does not expound be'asotah ["in doing it"] for this [purpose], rather to exempt an individual who acted upon a ruling of the court, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:3.hebrew: ור' יהודה פוטר - דלאו אורחיה בהכי, וסתם מתני' ר' יהודה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:3.english: And Rabbi Yehuda deems [them] exempt - Because it is not his [usual] way [to do it] in this manner, and the anonymous Mishnah is [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:4.hebrew: זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול - דאורחייהו להוציא בשנים, בהא סבירא ליה לרבי יהודה כרבי מאיר דחייב. ורבי שמעון פוטר, דיליף מקראי כדלקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:4.english: This [person] is incapable and that [person] is incapable - Since it is their normal way to carry [it] out by two [people], in this [case] Rabbi Yehuda holds like Rabbi Meir that [one is] liable. And Rabbi Shimon deems [them] exempt, as he derives [this] from verses, as [will be explained] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:5.hebrew: זה יכול וזה אינו יכול - והוציאו שניהן, דברי הכל חייב, ולקמן מפרש הי מינייהו חייב: ה"ג: הוציאוהו שנים — ר' מאיר מחייב, ול"ג פטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:11:5.english: This [one] is capable and that [one] is incapable - And both of them carried [it] out — everyone agrees [that he is] liable, and later [the Gemara] explains which one of them is liable. Thus we read [in the baraita]: "If two carried it out, Rabbi Meir deems [them] liable," and we do not read "exempt."

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר אם לא יכול אחד - כלומר כל אחד ואחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:1.english: Rabbi Yehudah says: If one is not able - That is to say, each and every one [of them is not able].

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:2.hebrew: ואם לאו - אלא זה יכול וזה יכול, פטור. וממילא דבכי האי גוונא ר' מאיר מחייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:2.english: And if not - Rather, [if] this one is able [to carry it out] and that one is able [to carry it out], [they are] exempt. And it follows by implication that in such a case, Rabbi Meir deems [them] liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:3.hebrew: מלגז - פורק"א בת ג' שיניים, ומהפכין בה תבואה בגורן, והוא מעמר, דהוא אב מלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:3.english: A pitchfork - Forche [Old French], [an implement] with three prongs, with which they turn over grain on the threshing floor; and this is [the labor of] gathering [sheaves], which is a primary category of labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:5.hebrew: בכרכר ושובטין - דהוא מיסך, כדאמר בפרק כלל גדול (לעיל שבת דף עה): שובט הרי הוא בכלל מיסך:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:5.english: With a shuttle and beating [the threads] - Which is [the labor of] stretching the warp, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Kelal Gadol (above, Shabbat 75): "Beating [the threads] is included in stretching the warp."

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:12:6.english: With a reed, and they carried it out, etc. - And all of these are [cases where] this one is able [to do it alone] and this one is able [to do it alone].

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:1.hebrew: המתכוין להוציא לפניו - כגון שצרר מעות בסדינו כדי שיהיו תלוין לפניו, ובא לו לאחריו:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:1.english: One who intends to carry out [an object] before him - For example, where he tied coins in his sheet so that they would hang before him, and it came [to be] behind him.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:2.hebrew: פטור - דלא נתקיימה מחשבתו, וה"ל כמתעסק ולא מתכוין:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:2.english: [He is] exempt - For his intention was not fulfilled, and he is like one acting unawares and not intentionally.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:3.hebrew: לאחריו ובא לו לפניו חייב - בגמ' מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:3.english: [If he intended to carry it] behind him and it came [to be] before him, he is liable - In the Gemara, [it] explains the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:4.hebrew: סינר - כעין מכנסיים קטנים, וחוגרת אותו לצניעות. ואם תלתה בו שום דבר להוציא, ובא לו לצד אחר — חייבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:4.english: Sinar - Like small breeches, and she girds it [around herself] for modesty. And if she hung something on it to carry [it] out, and it came to the other side, she is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:5.hebrew: שכן ראוי להיות חוזר - דרכו להיות חוזר סביבותיה, ומתחלתה ידעה שסופו להתהפך:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:5.english: As it is apt to turn around - Its nature is to turn around her, and from the outset she knew that it would eventually turn over.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:6.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר אף מקבלי פתקין - של מלך למוסרם לרצים, אף הם חייבים בהוצאתן אפילו לא נתקיימה מחשבתן, כגון הוציאן על מנת לתתן לרץ זה ונתנו לזה. כך לשון רבותי, ולבי מגמגם:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:2:6.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even those who receive notes - [Notes] of the king to deliver them to couriers — they too are liable for carrying them out even if their intention was not fulfilled, for example, [if] one carried them out in order to give them to this courier and gave them to another. Thus is the wording of my teachers, yet my heart hesitates.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:3:1.hebrew: מי ששנה זו לא שנה זו - ת"ק פטר בתרוייהו, ותנא בתרא מחייב בתרוייהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:3:1.english: He who taught this did not teach that - The first Tanna exempts in both [cases], and the latter Tanna holds [him] liable in both [cases].

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:3:2.hebrew: ועלתה בידו שמירה פחותה - ואנן סהדי דלא ניחא ליה, אבל סיפא כל שכן דניחא ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:3:2.english: And he ended up with reduced protection - And we are witnesses [i.e., it is obvious] that he is not pleased [with this], whereas [in] the latter case, all the more so is he pleased [with it].

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:4:1.hebrew: דיוקא דמתני' קשיא - דיוקא דמצינן למידק ממתני':
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:4:1.english: The inference of the Mishnah is difficult - [That is,] the inference that we can infer from the Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:4:2.english: Behind him, and it came [to be] before him, is [the case] where [he is] liable - For superior safeguarding came into his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:6:1.english: And the Sages deem [him] exempt - For this is not the manner of carrying out.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:7:1.english: I said one thing - "Do you not agree, etc."

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:7:2.hebrew: והם אמרו דבר א' - אי אתה מודה כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:7:2.english: And they said one thing - "Do you not agree," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:7:3.hebrew: מכלל דמחייב רבי יהודה - בתמיה. הא ודאי דברי הכל פטור, דלא מפקי אינשי הכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:7:3.english: Can it be inferred that Rabbi Yehuda deems [one] liable - [This is said] as a rhetorical question. For certainly everyone agrees [that he is] exempt, since people do not carry [objects] out in this manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:8:1.english: Behind him, and [it] came [to be carried out] behind him, everyone agrees [that he is] liable - For there are those who carry out [objects] in this manner, with inferior guarding.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:8:2.english: In a backhanded manner, everyone agrees [that he is] exempt - For [people] do not carry out [objects] in this manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:8:3.hebrew: מר מדמי לה לאחריו - דשמירה פחותה היא. ומר מדמי לה לאחר ידו, דלא דמי למוציא לאחריו, דהתם משתמרים הן מן הגנבים, אבל אלו נופלין מאליהן, ואין מוציאין כן:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:8:3.english: One Master likens it to [carrying] behind him - For it is an inferior [form of] guarding. And [the other] Master likens it to [carrying with] the back of his hand, for it is not similar to one who carries out behind him — for there they are guarded from thieves, whereas these fall out on their own, and people do not carry out [objects] in this manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 92b:9:1.hebrew: שכן לבלרי מלכות עושין כן - בדעתו למוסרן לזה ואין מוצאו, ודבר המלך נחוץ, ומצא אחר ומוסרו לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 92b:9:1.english: Because the royal scribes do this - [He] intends to hand them over to this [person], and he does not find him, and the king's matter is urgent, so he finds another [person] and hands it over to him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:11:1.hebrew: זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול ר"מ ורבי יהודה מחייבין - מה שהקשה ריב"א, אמאי לא אמרינן חטאת "אחד" אמר רחמנא ולא שנים ושלשה כדאמר גבי כופר — מפורש בפרק ד' וה' (ב"ק דף מ. ד"ה כופר):
Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:11:1.english: [If] this [person] is incapable and that [person] is incapable, Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda deem [them] liable - That which Riva asked — why do we not say [that with respect to] a sin-offering, the Merciful One said "one" and not two or three, as it says regarding ransom [kofer] — is explained in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah VaChamishah (Bava Kamma 40a, s.v. Kofer):

Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:1:1.hebrew: ואת"ל אנשי הוצל עושין כן, בטלה דעתן אצל כל אדם - משמע דעל אתרא נמי אמר דבטלה דעתן. וכן בריש בכל מערבין (עירובין דף כח.) פריך: "ובבל הוי רובא דעלמא? והתניא כו'", וכן בתר הכי פריך: "ופרסאי הוי רובא דעלמא?". וקשה, דבפ' חבית (לקמן שבת קמד:) גבי "של בית מנשיא היו סוחטים ברמונים", ופריך: "בית מנשיא הוי רובא דעלמא?", ומשני: "אין, דהתנן: המקיים קוצים בכרם כו', שכן בערביא מקיימין קוצים לגמליהן", ופריך: "מי דמי? ערביא אתרא הוא, הכא בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם!". וי"ל, דהתם חשוב מנהג ערביא, דלכל העולם נמי אם היה להם רוב גמלים הוו נמי מקיימי; אבל בית מנשיא דחד גברא — בטלה דעתו, אע"ג דלכל העולם אם היה להם רמונים הרבה היו סוחטין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:1:1.english: And if you say that the people of Hotzal do so, their intention is nullified by all people - This implies that even regarding a [whole] locality, [the Gemara] says that their intention is nullified. And similarly, at the beginning of [the chapter] Bekhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 28a), [the Gemara] asks: "And is Babylonia the majority of the world? Surely it was taught [in a baraita], etc.," and similarly after that it asks: "And are the Persians the majority of the world?" And this is difficult, for in the chapter Chavit (later, Shabbat 144b), regarding "Those of the household of Menashia would squeeze pomegranates," [the Gemara] asks: "Is the household of Menashia the majority of the world?" And it answers: "Yes, for we learned [in a Mishnah]: One who maintains thorns in a vineyard, etc., for in Arabia they maintain thorns for their camels." And [the Gemara] asks: "Is it comparable? Arabia is a locality, [whereas] here his intention is nullified by all people!" And one can answer that there it is considered the custom of Arabia, because for the entire world too, if they had many camels, they would also maintain [thorns]; whereas the household of Menashia, which is [only] a single person, his intention is nullified, even though for the entire world, if they had many pomegranates, they would squeeze [them].

Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:2:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר אף מקבלי פיתקין - מפרש רבינו שמואל שיש אדם ממונה למלך שנושא פיתקין של מלך לידע מנין גבוריו וחייליו ובית אוצרותיו, ונושאין אותן בכיסיהן התלויין באזוריהן, ואותן כיסין חוזרין פעמים לפניהן ופעמים לאחוריהן, והוי ממש דומיא דסינר דלעיל שהוא חוזר; ות"ק דר' יהודה לא חשיב ליה חוזר. והא דמייתי בגמרא: "תנא, שכן לבלרי מלכות עושין כן" — כלומר שחוזר, דבענין זה מיירי רישא (דברייתא) [דמתני']:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:2:1.english: Rabbi Yehudah says: Even those who receive notes [pittakin] - Rabbeinu Shmuel explains that there is a person appointed for the king who carries the king's notes to know the count of his mighty men, his soldiers, and his treasuries, and they carry them in their pouches that hang from their belts, and those pouches turn sometimes to their front and sometimes to their back; thus, it is literally like the sinar [mentioned] above, which turns around. And the Tanna Kamma [who disagrees with] Rabbi Yehudah does not consider it [something that] turns around. And that which is cited in the Gemara, "It was taught: For so do royal scribes do" — [this] means to say that it turns around, for it is regarding such a case that the first clause (of the Baraita) [of the Mishnah] speaks.

Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:3:1.hebrew: תברא מי ששנה זו כו' - ת"ק ה"ל למינקט "לאחריו ובא לו לפניו פטור", ולתנא בתרא דמחייב הוה לו למינקט "לפניו ובא לו לאחריו", דהוי רבותא טפי; אלא דהשתא לא ידע שיש בזה שום חילוק:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:3:1.english: [This mishna] is disjointed, he who taught this, etc. - The first Tanna should have stated, "[If he intended to carry it] behind him and it came before him, he is exempt," and the latter Tanna, who holds [him] liable, should have stated, "[If he intended to carry it] before him and it came behind him, [he is liable]," for that would be a greater novelty; however, at this point [Rabbi Elazar] did not know that there is any distinction in this [matter].

Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:4:1.hebrew: הא לאחריו ובא לאחריו פטור - לעיל (שבת דף צא:) גבי חזקיה משני "נעשה", ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף ה.) גבי "נתנה היא ואמרה היא"; ובכמה דוכתי לא משני:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92b:4:1.english: [By inference:] behind him, and it came behind him, he is exempt - Earlier (Shabbat 91b), regarding Chizkiyah, [the Gemara] answers "na'aseh" ([i.e.,] it is treated as though...), and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (5a), regarding "she gave [it] and she said [it]," [it likewise answers this way]; whereas in several [other] places it does not answer [in this manner].
